This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
is one step of the seminar. It ends with a **Do it** task and one set of
questions. The full explanations, examples and exercises are in the notes.

## Key terms

{{< glossary video-editor media-pool timeline playhead video-track video-clip split-clip trim-clip inspector export-preset >}}

## 20.1 A new project and the media pool

- A video editor never changes the source files; the **project** keeps the
  edits.
- First set the **resolution** and the **frame rate** (File › Project
  Settings): 1920 × 1080, 30 fps.
- **Import** the clips (File › Import › Media, or drag): they appear in the
  **media pool**.

![From a new project to an exported file.](images/workflow.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Moving the source files after the import gives "media offline".
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Your project"}
Make a project (1920 × 1080, 30 fps) and import three short clips of your
own or of a game you play.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · The project"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the Deliver page|the clip's name"}
where the imported clips appear
:   the media pool

what you set first in a new project
:   the resolution and the frame rate

what happens to the source files when you edit
:   nothing

why the editor shows "media offline"
:   the source files were moved
:::
:::

## 20.2 Viewer, inspector and timeline

- **Viewer:** the frame at the **playhead**. **Inspector:** settings of
  the selected clip.
- **Timeline:** time from left to right, on **tracks**.
- **V2** covers **V1**: a title on V2 is over the gameplay. Audio tracks
  play together.

![The Edit page.](images/editor-window.png){width=94%}

![Tracks on the timeline.](images/tracks.png){width=94%}

{{< sim file="sims/timeline-lab.html" poster="sims/timeline-lab.png" title="Timeline Lab: a first cut of the teaser" height="860" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A title on V1 after the clips plays on black, not over the picture.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Build the order"}
Put three clips on V1, a title on V2 at the start, and check it in the
viewer.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · The panels"}
Use Timeline Lab. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the media pool|A1"}
shows the frame at the playhead
:   the viewer

changes the size of the title
:   the inspector

the track for a title over the gameplay
:   V2

the line that marks the time in the viewer
:   the playhead
:::
:::

## 20.3 The four basic edits

- **Split** at the playhead (Blade **B**, or **Ctrl+B**).
- **Trim:** drag the start or the end of a clip.
- **Ripple delete:** delete and close the gap (Shift+Delete).
- **Move:** drag to another time or track. **Ctrl+Z** undoes.

![Four basic edits.](images/edit-tools.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A normal delete leaves a black gap.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Cut and tighten"}
Split a clip twice, ripple delete the middle, add music and trim it to the
end of the video.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Edits"}
Use Timeline Lab. Choose the edit.

::: {.match extra="export|import"}
cut a clip in two at 0:12
:   split

remove a part and close the gap
:   ripple delete

make the music end with the video
:   trim

put a clip on another track
:   move
:::
:::

## 20.4 A first export

- The project is not a video: **export** it (Deliver page, or File ›
  Export).
- **MP4**, **H.264**, the project's resolution and frame rate, a quality,
  a clear name with a version.
- Render, then watch the whole file once.

![The export settings.](images/export-settings.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Send the MP4, never the project file.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Export"}
Export `yourname-teaser-v1.mp4` (H.264, 1920 × 1080, 30 fps). Write its
length and size.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Export"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the project file|a GIF"}
the page that makes the video file
:   Deliver

the codec for a teaser for players
:   H.264

a good file name
:   rooftop-teaser-v1.mp4

after the render
:   watch the whole file once
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Editor Tour {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

The trainee asks seven questions: where the **imported clips** are, how to
**order** them, how to **cut** at 0:12, how to keep the **title over** the
gameplay, where to **resize** it, how to **remove a boring middle**, and
how to make an **MP4**.

{{< sim file="sims/editor-tour.html" poster="sims/editor-tour.png" title="Editor Tour: the right panel for each job" kind="game" height="600" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · The trainee's questions"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="rename the files|lower the volume"}
Where are the clips I just imported?
:   the media pool

How do I cut the boat clip at 0:12?
:   playhead to 0:12, then split

How do I keep the title over the gameplay?
:   put it on V2

How do I remove the boring middle without a gap?
:   ripple delete
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Set the resolution and frame rate first; imported clips go to the media
  pool.
- The viewer shows the playhead's frame; the inspector shows the selected
  clip.
- Higher video tracks cover lower ones; audio tracks play together.
- Split, trim, ripple delete and move build the edit.
- Export an MP4 with H.264, then watch it once.
